title: Before the Wedding
logline: In a provincial textile shop, weeks before a wedding, a family unfolds sari after sari, and one relative talks a hesitant bride into a colour she didn't choose.
human_question: When does choosing for someone else stop being help and start being your own wanting?

premise.story: A family's shopping day for a wedding: the bride, her mother, an aunt with strong opinions, and a shop assistant who has folded a thousand fabrics that week, ending in a bill and a decision that may or may not be the bride's own.
premise.place: A busy textile or saree shop in a provincial town during wedding season.
premise.experience: Colour, texture and light on fabric held up to faces; the small drama of a family choosing, differing and settling; the flat rhythm of the shop underneath it.

concept_links.why: This is the concept's own story seed: things seen as beautiful and reached for, with delight on one face and flat professional indifference on another [C004-M:L13] [C004-M:L17].
The bride's own eye lighting up is a spontaneous reaching; the aunt talking her into a different colour is the same wanting arising through another person's prompting [C006-M:L5] [C006-P:L44].

what_camera_could_observe: Fabric unfolded and held against a face
A relative arguing for a colour
The bride's hesitation and eventual choice
The shop assistant's practised, tired folding
The bill being written and counted
what_must_be_real: The family's actual shopping day, their own disagreements and the assistant's real working week. Nothing restaged for a better shot.

possible_arc.opening: Bolts of cloth unrolling under fluorescent light.
possible_arc.turn: A disagreement over colour, and someone gives way.
possible_arc.ending_open: The chosen sari is wrapped and paid for, or the family leaves without deciding. Reality decides.

position_hint: opening candidate: a clear image of wanting badly and being pulled by others' wanting too, with a natural moment for something small to be acquired if it genuinely becomes Object 2.

requirements: A textile or saree shop with a family genuinely shopping for a wedding
Consent from the family to be filmed choosing and disagreeing
A shop assistant willing to be filmed working

suggestions.name: A textile shop on the main street of Kurunegala
suggestions.why: A well-known provincial market town with a concentration of textile and saree shops serving surrounding villages.
suggestions.season_notes: Wedding seasons cluster around school holidays and after Vesak/Poson.
suggestions.verify: No shop or family has been contacted; this is a plausible town, not a confirmed location.

risks: Turning the family into a lesson about materialism
Making the aunt or assistant a comic figure without consent
Wedding pressure filmed as entertainment rather than lived experience
drop_if: No family will allow their real disagreements to be filmed
The shop will not allow filming during trading hours

connections.note: Two garments chosen for two different occasions, one led by others' wanting, one sorted by the customer's own reasons.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
